{"id":"jmap-chat-spec-qb21","title":"JMAP Chat has no language model: name/description/displayName/statusText/topic and message bodies carry no language, and clients can't ask for one","description":"Found 2026-11-14 while wiring mimid's JMAP Chat.name to MIMI room metadata (mimid bead mimid-1wgh.51), after a sweep of the MIMI drafts for English text that reaches users (IETF notes/2026-11-14-mimi-issues-from-table-draft.md, item 8).

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 says nothing about language anywhere. Human-readable properties with no language and no way to carry more than one:
- Chat: name (L599), description (L602), topic (L623, server-set)
- ChatContact: displayName (L525), statusText (L540)
- PresenceStatus: statusText (L1029)
- Space: name (L881), description (L884); Category: name (L847); SpaceRole: name (L799); CustomEmoji: name (L930)
- Endpoint and MessageAction label (L403, L426)
- Message: a body has bodyType but no language. MIMI content carries a per-part language (mimi-content-10), which a gateway drops; the rich body has a 'codeblock' lang (L1571) but that is a syntax hint, not the text's language.
Nor can a client say which language it wants (no request-side preference; JMAP has none generally).

Established pattern to reuse: JSCalendar RFC 8984 §4.2.8 locale (the language of the object's text) and §4.6.1 localizations (a map from language tag to PatchObject over the localizable properties), as used by JMAP Calendars. Proposal to work out:
1. Chat, Space, Category, SpaceRole, ChatContact, CustomEmoji gain optional locale and localizations.
2. Message gains an optional language (BCP 47) for the body, filled from mimi-content's part language by MIMI gateways.
3. Say whether a server MAY pick a localization for the client (e.g. from an account or session preference) or always returns all and lets the client choose. Prefer the latter (MAY, no MUST), in line with Mark's MAY > SHOULD > MUST preference.
4. Say that names are display text: servers and clients MUST NOT give them meaning (no matching on English role or space names), the same rule as proposed for MIMI room-policy.
Also check the companion drafts (mimi-00, federation-00, filenode-00) for the same gap.

{"description":"Found 2026-11-14 while wiring mimid's JMAP Chat.name to MIMI room metadata (mimid bead mimid-1wgh.51), after a sweep of the MIMI drafts for English text that reaches users (IETF notes/2026-11-14-mimi-issues-from-table-draft.md, item 8).

draft-atwood-jmap-chat-00 says nothing about language anywhere. Human-readable properties with no language and no way to carry more than one:
- Chat: name (L599), description (L602), topic (L623, server-set)
- ChatContact: displayName (L525), statusText (L540)
- PresenceStatus: statusText (L1029)
- Space: name (L881), description (L884); Category: name (L847); SpaceRole: name (L799); CustomEmoji: name (L930)
- Endpoint and MessageAction label (L403, L426)
- Message: a body has bodyType but no language. MIMI content carries a per-part language (mimi-content-10), which a gateway drops; the rich body has a 'codeblock' lang (L1571) but that is a syntax hint, not the text's language.
Nor can a client say which language it wants (no request-side preference; JMAP has none generally).

Established pattern to reuse: JSCalendar RFC 8984 §4.2.8 locale (the language of the object's text) and §4.6.1 localizations (a map from language tag to PatchObject over the localizable properties), as used by JMAP Calendars. Proposal to work out:
1. Chat, Space, Category, SpaceRole, ChatContact, CustomEmoji gain optional locale and localizations.
2. Message gains an optional language (BCP 47) for the body, filled from mimi-content's part language by MIMI gateways.
3. Say whether a server MAY pick a localization for the client (e.g. from an account or session preference) or always returns all and lets the client choose. Prefer the latter (MAY, no MUST), in line with Mark's MAY > SHOULD > MUST preference.
4. Say that names are display text: servers and clients SHOULD NOT give them meaning (no matching on English role or space names), the same rule as proposed for MIMI room-policy. SHOULD NOT, not MUST NOT: interop doesn't break without it (bcp14-keyword-discipline).
Scope widened 2026-11-15 (Mark: "encoding and locale stuff done the Right Thing as well"). Beyond language tags, settle these. Keyword strength per bcp14-keyword-discipline: MUST only where interop breaks; otherwise SHOULD, MAY or plain prose, and cite RFC 8620/7493 rather than restate.

5. Encoding. JMAP is already I-JSON (RFC 8620 s1.5 -> RFC 7493), so every string is UTF-8 with no lone surrogates. The per-property "MUST be valid UTF-8" text (login L523, body L706, subject L742, input validation L1755/L1763) restates that; replace it with one sentence citing RFC 8620 I-JSON. Keep the real distinction: a plaintext body is text; a ciphertext body is base64url and is never normalized or inspected.

6. Unicode normalization. Say what is (not) normalized: servers SHOULD NOT normalize message bodies or other user text they store and forward (signatures, E2EE, edit diffs). Compare identifiers and keys (reaction emoji L486, CustomEmoji name L931, login) as exact code-point sequences; say whether senders SHOULD send NFC. Reaction emoji: say how variation selectors (U+FE0F) and skin-tone sequences compare, or two clients' identical reactions don't aggregate.

7. Display names and spoofing. displayName, Chat/Space/Category/SpaceRole name are free-form display text. Consider RFC 8266 (PRECIS nicknames) as a SHOULD for enforcement/comparison of displayName, and RFC 8264 IdentifierClass or plain ASCII for login and shortcodes (CustomEmoji is already ASCII lowercase; say so is deliberate). Security Considerations: confusables and bidi overrides in names (UTS #39, UAX #9); clients SHOULD isolate bidi when interpolating a name into UI text (FSI/PDI or <bdi>).

8. Lengths. maxBodyBytes (L327) is in UTF-8 octets; good. Say every length limit is in octets, and that a server truncating anything (previews, notification text, lastMessage snippets, push payloads) SHOULD cut on a grapheme-cluster boundary (UAX #29), never mid-code-point.

9. Collation and sorting. Space/query and others default-sort by name ascending (L1402, L1495) and ChatContact sorts by login, with no collation. JMAP RFC 8620 s5.5 Comparator has a 'collation' argument (RFC 4790 registry; i;unicode-casemap RFC 5051 is the JMAP default). Say name sorts honour Comparator.collation, and list collations in the capability (as JMAP Mail does with collationAlgorithms) so a client can ask for a locale-aware one.

10. Time and time zones. Wire timestamps are UTCDate (fine; no locale on the wire). Any wall-clock or recurring times (muteUntil is absolute, fine; any future quiet hours / DND schedule / Calendars and Tasks companions) SHOULD carry an IANA time zone ID, as JSCalendar does. Date/number formatting is client-side presentation; say so once.

11. Text search. Where a filter does text matching (Message text filters, ChatContact/Space name filters), say matching is case-insensitive per the collation and that stemming/tokenization is language-dependent and implementation-defined; a Message language (item 2) lets a server pick the analyzer.

12. Server-generated text. Any human-readable string the server writes (system messages, topic L623, error 'description' in SetErrors, RFC 9457 problem 'detail' per jmap-chat-spec-hl0h) is for debugging or display only, never parsed; servers MAY localize it using Accept-Language on the HTTP request (RFC 9110 s12.5.4) or a session preference, and SHOULD tag it with a language when they do.

Also check the companion drafts (mimi-00, federation-00, filenode-00, calendars-00, tasks-00, push-00, wss-00) for the same gaps; federation must carry language/localizations across servers unchanged, and push payloads hit the truncation and bidi points.

Unblocks mimid-1wgh.51, which should implement whatever this settles rather than inventing an Accept-Language rule.
","title":"JMAP Chat i18n: no language model, and encoding/normalization/collation/locale rules unsettled"}
